seriesPage.title: Series
seriesPage.subtitle: Prestige ranking and d-index weights · {year}
seriesPage.prestigeLead: Selected championships ranked by difficulty relative to each other. The higher this measure, the harder it is to win in that series compared with the others. Difficulty feeds directly into Drift Index (d-index).

colHelp.rank: Series position in the prestige ranking. Higher Hardness means a higher Rank.
colHelp.series: Featured championship included in prestige and d-index calculations.
colHelp.hardness: Reflects the average difference in places a driver takes compared with their results in other series; based on places at each event, not season standings. It is a scale, not a coefficient — it shows the average gap between places held.
colHelp.samples: Drivers who competed in multiple series; hardness is calculated from their results.

overlap.title: 1. Series difficulty (Hardness)
overlap.body: We compare pilots who race in more than one featured series. If their average finish is worse in one championship than in the others, that series is rated tougher. Hardness ranks featured series from most to least difficult.

p4p.title: 2. Drift Index
p4p.body: Each driver's score comes from their season in featured series: average event place, missed rounds, qualifying level, and how hard that series is. A strong result in a tougher championship weighs more. We take the best series result; racing in extra featured series adds a small bonus. Higher index points means a stronger season.

indexPoints.title: 3. Event results
indexPoints.body: Every round is converted to a comparable score from finishing position and how deep the qualifying grid was that weekend. That keeps events fair when entry lists differ in size.

noData.title: 4. Series without crossover
noData.body: If nobody from a featured series also appears in our other tracked championships, we cannot estimate its difficulty. Those series stay in the prestige table but are left out of Drift Index until crossover data exists.
